haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store, never charging.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days below 0.1 percent mismatch and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes and approves the move.
haiku-low.q4: A new-engine charge failure rate above 2 percent in any 10-minute window. It can happen in both or new_only, not shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only with gates reset. Returning to shadow requires a person. The new engine's takeover conditions are otherwise NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q6: After day 35 in new_only, because the usage event log keeps only 35 days and the skipped events needed for rollback age out.
haiku-low.q7: How billing workers learn the mode is an open question, so NOT STATED. What happens to an invoice mid-processing is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Where gate evidence is kept is NOT STATED; a rollout record is only recommended, an open decision. The rollout controller refuses a forward move until its gate is met.
haiku-low.q9: The rollout controller detects it, measuring new-engine charge failure rate above 2 percent over any 10-minute window. When met, it starts RB1 on its own.
haiku-low.q10: Customers get no new charges and due invoices wait, as in a stall. Due charges are made in RB3, after RB2 reconciliation completes.
haiku-low.q11: RB3 charges only due invoices with no successful charge. Ledger or provider status under the idempotency key shows success, so invoices already charged are skipped.
haiku-low.q12: Mode stays both or new_only, charging frozen, step recorded. Failed RB2 enters rb_stalled, exited by a fix resuming RB2 or signed-off manual reconciliation.

sonnet.q1: The old engine still charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store; it never charges or writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging, so it stays current and can take over.
sonnet.q3: The gate: 7 consecutive days below 0.1 percent mismatch and at least 5000 invoices compared. A person makes and approves the move (the controller refuses it until the gate is met).
sonnet.q4: A new-engine charge failure rate above 2 percent in any 10-minute window. It applies in both and new_only (the controller starts RB1). Not in shadow, and not in retired.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, with all gates reset. To take over again, a person must move to shadow and the whole gate sequence restarts (7-day count starts over).
sonnet.q6: After day 35 in new_only. The skipped usage events age out of the 35-day usage event log, and rollback needs them. After that the old engine can be retired with no way back.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED. The document lists as open how engines learn billing_mode (read each run or pushed), and says nothing about an invoice being processed at that moment.
sonnet.q8: Gate evidence (the rollout record with streak and day counters) is not specified in the brief; the recommendation is one rollout record next to billing_mode. The rollout controller refuses a forward move until its gate is met. How enforcement works (e.g. direct flag setting) is open.
sonnet.q9: The rollout controller (not written yet). It watches the new-engine charge failure rate over any 10-minute window; when it is above 2 percent in both or new_only, it starts RB1 on its own.
sonnet.q10: No new charges are sent during RB1 and RB2; due invoices wait, delayed not dropped. They are charged in RB3 by the old engine, once each, only for invoices that are due and have no successful charge.
sonnet.q11: RB3 only charges invoices without a successful charge, where the ledger or the provider shows one under the idempotency key (customer, billing period, invoice). RB1 also never re-sends a charge and looks up unknown statuses first.
sonnet.q12: If RB2 reconcile fails, the rollback enters rb_stalled: billing_mode stays both or new_only, new-engine charging stays frozen, old engine does not charge, and due charges are delayed. On-call escalates. It continues by a fix and resume of RB2, or a signed-off per-invoice manual reconciliation into RB3.
